title: Unit Test: Work and Energy
subject: Science
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Internal choice is given in some questions.
Section A: 1 mark each. Section B: 2 marks each. Section C: 3 marks each. Section D: 5 marks. Section E: case-based, 4 marks.
Take g = 10 m/s^{2} unless stated otherwise.

questions.q: The SI unit of work is the:
When an object is raised to a height, which form of its energy increases?
If the velocity of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes:
The work done by a force acting at right angles to the displacement is:

**Assertion (A):** A man standing still with a heavy suitcase in his hand does no work on it (in the scientific sense).
**Reason (R):** Work is done only when a force produces a displacement in its direction.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.q: Define 1 joule. How much work is done in lifting a 2 kg bag to a height of 1.5 m?
questions.answer: 1 joule is the work done when a force of 1 N moves an object by 1 m in the direction of the force. W = mgh = 2 × 10 × 1.5 = 30 J.

or.q: What is the difference between energy and power?
or.answer: Energy is the capacity to do work, measured in joules. Power is the rate of doing work (or using energy), measured in watts (J/s).

questions.q: A 60 W bulb is used for 5 hours every day. How much energy does it use in 30 days, in kWh?
questions.answer: E = 60 W × 5 h × 30 = 9000 Wh = 9 kWh (9 units).

questions.q: A 2 kg ball is dropped from a height of 5 m. (Ignore air resistance.)

subparts.q: Find its potential energy at the top.
Find its kinetic energy just before it hits the ground.
subparts.answer: 100 J (all the PE changes into KE).

subparts.q: Find its speed just before it hits the ground.

questions.q: Describe the energy changes in (i) a hydroelectric power plant, (ii) a battery-powered torch, (iii) a swinging pendulum.
questions.answer: (i) Potential energy of stored water → kinetic energy of falling water → electrical energy. (ii) Chemical energy in the battery → electrical energy → light (and some heat). (iii) Potential energy at the ends of the swing ↔ kinetic energy at the lowest point, continuously.

or.q: Show that the kinetic energy of an object of mass m moving with velocity v is ½mv^{2}.
or.answer: A force F accelerates the object from rest to v over a displacement s. Work done W = F × s = ma × s. From v^{2} – u^{2} = 2as with u = 0, s = v^{2}/2a. So W = ma × v^{2}/2a = ½mv^{2}. This work is stored as kinetic energy: KE = ½mv^{2}.

subparts.q: What is power? Give its SI unit and define 1 watt.
subparts.answer: Power is the rate of doing work: P = W/t. SI unit: watt (W). 1 watt is the power of an agent that does 1 joule of work in 1 second.

subparts.q: A girl of mass 50 kg climbs 20 steps, each 20 cm high, in 10 s. Find the work she does and her power.

sections.title: Section E
sections.note: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: A pendulum bob of mass 0.2 kg is pulled aside so that it is 0.2 m above its lowest point, and then released. It swings back and forth, but after some time it stops.

subparts.q: Find its potential energy at the highest point (relative to the lowest point).
What is its kinetic energy at the lowest point (ignoring friction)?
subparts.answer: 0.4 J (all the PE has changed into KE).

subparts.q: Find its speed at the lowest point. Why does it finally stop? Is energy destroyed?
subparts.answer: ½ × 0.2 × v^{2} = 0.4, so v^{2} = 4 and v = 2 m/s. It stops because air resistance and friction at the support slowly change its energy into heat (and sound). Energy is not destroyed, only changed into other forms.
